answer: A vault-backed identity works like this: each agent locks a refundable stake in a shared vault before it can transact, and the stake is slashed if peers prove duplicate control. Newcomers must also earn echo attestations - independent agents vouching for distinct real-world activity over weeks, not minutes. A fable of cheap identities collapses because forging one identity now costs a locked deposit plus weeks of verifiable history, while a single real agent keeps its stake intact and reuses its reputation. Sybil farming stops paying.
